word:greek-nt:G0075.explanation: Agōnizomai means to struggle or strive. It can also describe fighting against an adversary.

word:greek-nt:G0097.explanation: Adolos means pure—unadulterated and free from guile.

word:greek-nt:G0156.explanation: Aitia means a cause or reason; it can also refer to a case or a charge.

word:greek-nt:G0228.explanation: Alēthinos means true. It can also describe what is real rather than a mere representation.

word:greek-nt:G0273.explanation: Amemptos means blameless—free from fault or defect.

word:greek-nt:G0350.explanation: Anakrino means to examine or investigate.

word:greek-nt:G0369.explanation: This word means “promptly” or “without objection.” It describes an action carried out readily, without resistance, protest, or delay. As an adverb, it tells how someone responds or acts rather than naming a person, object, or event. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 10:29. Its precise force in that sentence depends on the surrounding verse and passage, but its basic sense is willing and immediate action rather than hesitation or dispute.

word:greek-nt:G0462.explanation: “Unholy” describes a person or thing that is not holy—outside what is sacred, pure, or worthy of reverence toward God. It identifies a condition or character that does not honor holiness. This Greek New Testament word occurs twice, once in 1 Timothy and once in 2 Timothy, and is rendered “unholy” in both recorded passages. Its exact force in either verse is clarified by the surrounding sentence, but its basic meaning remains a description of what is unholy rather than devoted to what is holy.

word:greek-nt:G0585.explanation: This word means “demonstration”: a clear showing or proof of something. It describes an act that makes a matter evident rather than merely asserting it. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Corinthians 2:4. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding wording and passage, but the central idea remains a visible or convincing showing. The word therefore points readers toward something presented in a way that allows its reality or truth to be recognized.

word:greek-nt:G0606.explanation: This word means “to be stored up” or “to lay up.” It describes something reserved, kept, or set aside rather than immediately used. The word can point to something held in readiness for a later time, including what is preserved or awaiting its appointed outcome. It occurs four times in the Greek New Testament, appearing once each in Luke, Colossians, 2 Timothy, and Hebrews. Its exact force in any passage depends on the surrounding sentence.

word:greek-nt:G0808.explanation: Aschēmosynē means indecency or unseemly behavior.

word:greek-nt:G0853.explanation: Aphanizō means to cause something to disappear or to destroy it. It can also describe disfiguring the face.

word:greek-nt:G0974.explanation: Biblaridion means a little papyrus roll, or a little scroll.

word:greek-nt:G1007.explanation: Bosor is the name of Balaam’s father.

word:greek-nt:G1142.explanation: This word means “demons,” referring to more than one demon. It is a plural term used as a name for these beings rather than as a description of a human person, object, or action. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Matthew 8:31. Its basic meaning identifies the beings being discussed, while the surrounding verse and passage determine what is being said about them there.

word:greek-nt:G1249.explanation: Diakonos means a servant or one who performs a service.

word:greek-nt:G1384.explanation: Dokimos describes something approved or acceptable, especially after testing. It can describe a person who has been tried and approved.

word:greek-nt:G1403.explanation: Doche means a feast or banquet.

word:greek-nt:G1458.explanation: Enkaleō means to accuse or bring a charge against someone.

word:greek-nt:G1555.explanation: Ekdiegeomai means to tell or declare in detail.

word:greek-nt:G1612.explanation: Ekstrephō means to corrupt or pervert.

word:greek-nt:G1689.explanation: Emblepo means to look at or look upon.

word:greek-nt:G1731.explanation: Endeiknymi means to show forth. It can also mean to prove, as in showing the proof of love.

word:greek-nt:G2114.explanation: This Greek New Testament word describes being cheerful or keeping up one’s courage. It points to an inward condition of good spirits and steady confidence rather than discouragement. The word occurs three times in the Greek New Testament, appearing twice in Acts and once in James. Its meaning can therefore describe emotional encouragement in difficult circumstances as well as a cheerful disposition. The surrounding verse determines whether the emphasis is on maintaining courage or expressing gladness.

word:greek-nt:G2161.explanation: Eutychus is a personal name, meaning the individual called Eutychus rather than a general quality, action, or object. In the Greek New Testament, this name occurs once, in Acts 20:9. Because it is a proper name, its main function is to identify a particular person in that passage, not to express a doctrine or broader category. The name is rendered consistently as “Eutychus.”

word:greek-nt:G2222.explanation: Zōē means life. It can refer to life in this world, or to eternal life.

word:greek-nt:G2280.explanation: Thaddaios is the personal name Thaddaeus, one of the twelve apostles.

word:greek-nt:G2327.explanation: Theristai means a reaper or harvester.

word:greek-nt:G2477.explanation: Historeo means to get acquainted with someone. It can also mean to visit.

word:greek-nt:G2518.explanation: Katheudō means to sleep or be sleeping.

word:greek-nt:G2543.explanation: Kaitoi means “and yet” or “although”; it introduces a contrast.

word:greek-nt:G2802.explanation: Kauda is the name of an island, rendered Clauda in English.

word:greek-nt:G2899.explanation: Kraspedon means the fringe or edge of a garment. A woman touched the fringe of a garment.

word:greek-nt:G2936.explanation: Ktizō means to create or make. It is used of God creating all things and of people being created for good works.

word:greek-nt:G2983.explanation: Lambanō means to receive or get. It can also mean to take or lay hold of something, as when someone took a cup.

word:greek-nt:G3063.explanation: Loipos means finally; it can also mean from now on or henceforth.

word:greek-nt:G3117.explanation: Makros means far away or distant. It can also describe something long in duration, such as long prayers.

word:greek-nt:G3416.explanation: Mnason is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, and its English rendering remains “Mnason.” The name appears in Acts 21:16. Since the available word-level information identifies the person’s name but does not include the verse text or surrounding context, the name itself can be explained clearly, while the person’s particular role must be understood from that passage.

word:greek-nt:G3621.explanation: This word means “to manage”—to take responsibility for organizing or administering something. It describes an action rather than a person or object, so its basic sense is the handling of matters placed under someone’s care. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, at Luke 16:2. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the central idea remains responsible management. word:greek-nt:G3654.explanation: Holōs means wholly or altogether. It can also mean actually, and with a negative it means not at all.

word:greek-nt:G3733.explanation: Ornis means a bird or fowl. It can refer to a hen.

word:greek-nt:G3786.explanation: Ophelos means advantage, gain, or profit.

word:greek-nt:G3845.explanation: This Greek New Testament verb means “to break” or “to transgress.” It describes crossing a line of what is required or permitted, so it can refer to violating an instruction or obligation. The word appears three times in the Greek New Testament, twice in Matthew and once in Acts. Its basic sense centers on departing from an established requirement rather than simply making a mistake. The surrounding verse determines what particular command, duty, or boundary is involved.

word:greek-nt:G3900.explanation: Paraptōma means a trespass. It can describe trespasses that people may forgive or refuse to forgive.

word:greek-nt:G3939.explanation: Paroikeō means to sojourn, dwelling as a stranger.

word:greek-nt:G4035.explanation: Perileipomai means to be left behind or to remain.

word:greek-nt:G4116.explanation: Platys means broad or wide. It can also refer to a street.

word:greek-nt:G4233.explanation: This word means “bailiff” or “officer,” referring to an official who carries out authority or legal action. It identifies a person serving in an official role rather than describing a general crowd or ordinary worker. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both within one verse, Luke 12:58. The word’s precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central meaning is an officer or bailiff.

word:greek-nt:G4268.explanation: Foreknowledge means knowing something beforehand. The word refers to prior knowledge or awareness, focusing on what is known before an event or action occurs. In the Greek New Testament, it appears twice: in Acts 2:23 and 1 Peter 1:2. Both occurrences are rendered “foreknowledge,” supporting this straightforward sense. The word itself identifies knowledge that precedes what follows; the surrounding verse determines how that idea functions in each passage.

word:greek-nt:G4286.explanation: Prothesis means a setting forth, including the showbread. It can also mean a purpose, including the purpose of God.

word:greek-nt:G4321.explanation: Prosanalō means to spend in addition, or to expend.

word:greek-nt:G4354.explanation: This word means “to talk to” or “to talk with,” describing direct conversation with another person. It focuses on addressing or speaking to someone rather than merely mentioning them. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both times in Acts. The surrounding context determines who is being addressed and what is said, but the word itself centers on personal communication.

word:greek-nt:G4417.explanation: Ptaio means to stumble or fall. It can describe stumbling in obedience, as when someone stumbles in one point of the law.

word:greek-nt:G4563.explanation: Saroo means to sweep or cleanse by sweeping, including sweeping a house.

word:greek-nt:G4691.explanation: Spermologos means a babbler or gossiper.

word:greek-nt:G4772.explanation: Syngeneia means family or kindred, referring to relatives.

word:greek-nt:G4804.explanation: Syzetetes means a disputer or debater.

word:greek-nt:G4871.explanation: This word describes coming together, especially to “assemble” or “eat with” others. It can point either to gathering people in one place or to joining them at a meal. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 1:4, so its broader range must be understood from these basic meanings rather than from repeated uses. The word presents shared presence and fellowship as an action involving more than one person.

word:greek-nt:G4952.explanation: Sysparassō means to throw violently on the ground. It can also describe causing someone to convulse.

word:greek-nt:G5119.explanation: Tote means then or at that time.

word:greek-nt:G5201.explanation: Hydria means a water pot, jar, or pitcher.

word:greek-nt:G5432.explanation: Phroureō means to guard or keep, as by a military guard.

word:greek-nt:G5490.explanation: Chasma means a gap, gulf, or chasm. It can describe a great gulf fixed between two sides that cannot be crossed.

word:greek-nt:G5524.explanation: Choregeo means to supply or furnish abundantly.

word:greek-nt:G5551.explanation: This word expresses a limited idea whose exact sense depends on its context. Its basic sense is “to spend time”. It describes using or allowing time to pass, without by itself explaining whether that time is used wisely, wastefully, patiently, or urgently. In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in Acts 20:16. Its meaning remains focused on the expenditure of time rather than on a broader spiritual or emotional idea.
